body: Input (stripped of personal context): an 8-row table comparing AuDHD vs fearful-avoidant (FA) patterns across communication, work, decisions, intimacy, conflict, insight, support, regulation, plus a 'core dynamic' and 'tragedy' conclusion. Steps run: 1, 2, 3, 6. Step 1: closing conclusion ('neither can sustain the conditions for change without external structure neither can provide') halts NOT EVEN WRONG — any change gets credited to 'external structure', so no outcome counts against it. Step 2: restated (steelman) — table treats AuDHD and FA as two separate partners, but they are traits one person can hold together; FA is treated as a fixed category though adult attachment is measured on two continuous dimensions (anxiety, avoidance). Step 3: no sources; reads as generated synthesis. Decision-making row ('felt sense, internal timing'; 'borrows external urgency') and insight row ('shame collapses insight') have no literature behind them; 'felt sense' runs against the alexithymia/interoception findings common in autism. Regulation row contradicts itself: both columns describe needing space, yet the combined column says one needs presence. Step 6: intimacy-overwhelm, approach-avoidance, real-time processing, shutdown rows point at real findings but are written as universal with no magnitude. Measurement confound: autistic traits correlate with higher self-reported avoidance and anxiety on attachment scales, so the two columns may double-count one thing. Falsifier: couples with this mix who adopt structure (async/written check-ins, couples therapy) and show sustained change would falsify the fatalistic close.
plain: Screened a generated table pairing AuDHD and fearful-avoidant attachment patterns in relationships; rows are overstated and the closing 'tragedy' conclusion is unfalsifiable as framed.

verdict.value: OVERSTATED at step 6 (table); NOT EVEN WRONG at step 1 (closing conclusion); restated at 2, unsupported rows at 3
